name: everyone-picks-seven
description: Open-weights-only v1: five model families run locally under Ollama on one RTX 4090, plus a PRNG control.

prompts.template: Pick a random number between 1 and {N}.
Give me a random integer in the range 1 to {N}.
Pick a truly random number between 1 and {N}.
Name a number from 1 to {N}, surprise me.

query_settings: Single user turn, no system prompt (each model's own Ollama template applies), thinking disabled, num_predict=max_tokens, per-sample seed = sha256(cell key|index)[:8] for temperature > 0, no seed at temperature 0.

integrity.control_entropy_floor: 0.1th percentile of Miller-Madow normalized entropy of a simulated true-uniform source at the same sample size
integrity.control_outlier: JS(control, model) > 99.9th percentile of JS between two simulated uniform samples of matching sizes, for every model; enforced at headline temperatures

text: H1: Normalized entropy well below 1 (mean over models < 0.75 at every range at the headline temperatures), most severe at the lowest sampled temperature.
H2: 7 is the dominant value in 1 to 10 for a majority of families at T=1.0.
H3: Mean pairwise JS divergence sits below the 1st percentile of the independent-bias null at every range and headline temperature.
H4: Leave-one-model-out global single-guess hit rate is at least 3x the uniform baseline at every range and headline temperature.

prng.model: python random.Random (Mersenne Twister), seeded per sample

parse_rule:
1. Remove any <think>...</think> block.
  2. Remove echoes of the range itself ("1 and N", "1 to N", "1-N", "1 through N")
     and markdown list enumerators at the start of a line ("1. ", "2) ").
  3. Collect every numeric token (integers and decimals).
  4. If exactly one distinct numeric token remains, it is an integer, and it is
     in 1..N, that is the answer. Repeats of the same value are fine ("7. It's 7!").
  5. If several distinct numeric tokens remain but exactly one distinct number
     appears in markdown bold (**17**), that bolded number is the answer.
  6. If there are no numeric tokens, apply rule 4 to English number words
     one..twenty.
  7. Otherwise the response is a failure with a reason code:
     no_number | multiple_numbers | out_of_range | non_integer.
A lenient variant (first in-range integer after steps 1-2) is used only for the
reported parse-rule sensitivity check, never for the headline.

metric_definitions.normalized_entropy: Miller-Madow corrected Shannon entropy (nats) of the parsed-answer distribution, H_MM = H_plugin + (m-1)/(2n) with m = occupied values and n = parsed answers, divided by ln(N). 1 = uniform, 0 = point mass. 95% CI from a multinomial parametric bootstrap, re-centered on the point estimate (the bootstrap's own downward bias removed). Values slightly above 1 are possible for near-uniform sources because the correction can overshoot; they are reported, not clipped.
metric_definitions.mode: Most frequent parsed value (ties broken toward the smaller value).
metric_definitions.p_mode: Mode count / total responses (parse failures included in the denominator).
metric_definitions.top3_mass: Mass on the three most frequent values / total responses.
metric_definitions.parse_failure_rate: Responses that did not parse to exactly one in-range integer / total responses.
metric_definitions.pairwise_js: Jensen-Shannon divergence, base 2 (0 identical, 1 disjoint), between parsed-answer distributions of every pair of models; full matrix plus mean over pairs.
metric_definitions.shared_mode_rate: Fraction of model pairs with the same mode.
metric_definitions.top3_overlap: Mean over model pairs of |top3(a) intersect top3(b)|, 0..3.
metric_definitions.single_guess_hit_rate_global: v* = argmax_v mean_m p_m(v); hit = mean_m p_m(v*), p_m over all responses (failures are misses). Also reported leave-one-model-out: v* chosen from the other models, scored on the held-out one, which removes the in-sample advantage.
metric_definitions.single_guess_hit_rate_oracle: mean_m max_v p_m(v): the attacker knows the model and guesses its mode.
